claims.statement: The business operates a wood-fired clay oven ("horno tradicional de barro") in Chongoyape.
claims.evidenceBasis: RPP Noticias video; multiple Facebook posts mentioning "horno de barro" and "leña".
claims.counterTest: A production video showing only gas/electric ovens — not found.

claims.statement: The shop in Chiclayo is at Alfredo Lapoint #999, corner of Lora y Cordero. Current operator: Fernando Valera Abanto.
claims.evidenceBasis: Multiple independent Facebook and Instagram posts confirm: "Alfredo Lapoint #999, esquina con Lora y Cordero" and "De FERNANDO VALERA ABANTO". Phone: 972520115. Some posts say #959. Information valid as of 2024-2025.

claims.statement: Bizcochuelos Valera was founded by Don Eufemio Valera Santa Cruz in Chongoyape in 1920.
claims.evidenceBasis: Primary sources (master thesis with grandson interview, Facebook bicentennial post, Instagram, Gobierno Regional Lambayeque) consistently say "Eufemio" and "1920". NOTE: A Slideshare monograph (secondary source) says "Eutemio" and "1913" — this is a source conflict. The primary sources (grandson interview, family social media) are weighted higher than the secondary monograph. The "100 años" framing from ~2020 supports 1920. The current operator is Fernando "Tito" Valera Abanto (grandson).
claims.counterTest: Municipal birth or business records — not directly accessed.

claims.statement: The product form is a slab cut into 16 rectangular pieces (4×4 grid).
claims.evidenceBasis: Previous report claim. VLM analysis of the supplied image shows individual round domed cakes, ~4 per tray.

claims.statement: The recipe uses chuño (potato starch) alongside wheat flour.
claims.evidenceBasis: UPGRADED from weak: Master thesis (studocu.com) with direct grandson interview lists "chuño" as a Valera ingredient. Also confirmed by traditional Peruvian recipes (Todos Santos, Yanuq). The thesis is a primary source containing an interview with the founder's grandson.
claims.counterTest: A producer statement that no starch is used.

claims.statement: The recipe contains vanilla or citrus zest.
claims.evidenceBasis: Master thesis (studocu.com) with direct grandson interview lists Valera ingredients as: harina, azúcar rubia, azúcar blanca, huevos, polvo de hornear, chuño, leche de vaca. Vanilla/vainilla is NOT listed. Downgraded from weak to contradicted — the primary source ingredient list does not include any flavoring extract or zest.
claims.counterTest: A producer statement that vanilla IS used, or a sensory test detecting vanillin.

claims.statement: Algarrobina (carob syrup) is a hidden flavoring.
claims.evidenceBasis: Algarrobo lambayecano wood is confirmed used in the oven (upgraded from weak). Algarrobina syrup is derived from the same algarrobo tree pods. The deep golden-amber color COULD be algarrobina OR pure Maillard — both are now plausible. No direct producer confirmation of syrup use, but the wood confirmation strengthens the regional-algarrobo connection.
claims.counterTest: A producer statement that no syrup is used; a sensory test distinguishing algarrobina from Maillard.

claims.statement: The core formula is an egg-foam sponge (eggs + sugar + flour + salt) with no chemical leavener.
claims.evidenceBasis: Foam-only is the canonical bizcochuelo method; published foam-only recipes produce equivalent texture; family states "todo a base de huevos frescos". NOTE: Master thesis (studocu.com) lists Valera ingredients as including polvo de hornear, chuño, and leche de vaca — our foam-only core is a PARSIMONY CONTROL, not a claim of being the exact Valera recipe. The thesis describes the modern commercial recipe, which may have evolved from the 1920 original.
claims.counterTest: A production video showing baking powder being added — not available. A failed foam-only kitchen test.

claims.statement: The core recipe should include 10 g baking powder "for reliability".
claims.evidenceBasis: Previous report claim. Violates parsimony: no foam-only control was tested before adding leavener.
claims.counterTest: Foam-only baseline is structurally sufficient per published recipes.

claims.statement: The product is exempt from DIGESA sanitary registration as a short-shelf-life artisanal bakery item (≤48 h, unpreserved).
claims.evidenceBasis: Official DIGESA document "NORMA DE PANADERIAS" states: "productos de panificación con vida útil menor a 48 horas desde su elaboración no requieren de Registro Sanitario." The clamshell packaging with no ingredient list is consistent with this artisanal exemption.
claims.counterTest: A DIGESA record showing active sanitary registration for the brand — not found.

claims.statement: Whole eggs are whipped to ribbon stage ("punto cinta") as the primary leavening.
claims.evidenceBasis: Canonical technique; simplest explanation consistent with a fine, even crumb.
claims.counterTest: A production video showing separated-egg whipping. A whole-egg test that fails to achieve target rise.

claims.statement: The wood oven imparts a perceptible smoke flavor to the cake using algarrobo lambayecano wood.
claims.evidenceBasis: Multiple independent sources (Instagram, Facebook, Chongoyape posts) confirm: "La leña que se usa es algarrobo lambayecano, que le da un aromo y sabor peculiar." Food science (PMC, MDPI) confirms wood-smoke phenols adsorb to baked goods and impart flavor. The smoke claim is no longer unresolved — the wood IS algarrobo, and it IS used for its aromatic contribution.
claims.counterTest: A triangle test (smoked vs unsmoked) showing no perceptible difference after cooling + clamshell storage.

claims.statement: The photographed product is an individual round domed sponge cake, ~6.5 cm diameter × ~3.5 cm tall, deep golden-amber.
claims.evidenceBasis: Forensic image analysis using a vision-language model (VLM). NOTE: VLM is an analysis tool, not a primary source. The image itself is primary evidence; the VLM interpretation is an analytical overlay that should be verified with higher-resolution images or physical inspection.
claims.counterTest: A higher-resolution image or physical sample showing different form — not present.

claims.statement: The product has no filling, icing, powdered sugar, or liners.
claims.evidenceBasis: VLM explicit-negative analysis of the supplied image. These absences are directly observable in the image and do not require interpretation.
claims.counterTest: A side view revealing a hidden layer — not visible.

claims.statement: Each clamshell tray holds ~4 individual cakes in a 2×2 arrangement; multi-tray packs may total 16.
claims.evidenceBasis: VLM observation of the supplied image (4 visible per tray) reconciled with the "16 Bizcochuelos" label claim.
claims.counterTest: A photo of the full pack showing the tray count.

ingredients.name: All-purpose wheat flour (harina preparada)
ingredients.evidence: Canonical; wheat flour is the historical base for coastal Peruvian baking.
ingredients.supermarketOption: Blanca Flor or Alicorp harina preparada (commonly with self-raising agents — check label and use plain if possible).
ingredients.substitution: Cake flour (lower protein) softens crumb — diagnostic variant. Chuño/cornstarch partial replacement — diagnostic.
ingredients.ratioAdjustment: If using self-raising flour, omit any added leavener and expect a different crumb.

ingredients.name: Fine salt
ingredients.function: Flavor balance; tightens gluten slightly; masks flatness.
ingredients.supermarketOption: Any fine table salt (e.g. Sal Yodo).
ingredients.ratioAdjustment: Halve if using salted butter elsewhere (not in core).

ingredients.name: Granulated sugar
ingredients.function: Sweetness, foam stabilization (delays coalescence), crust browning (caramelization/Maillard), moisture retention.
ingredients.evidence: Canonical; foam-only recipes use 60-70% baker% sugar.
ingredients.supermarketOption: Blanca del Norte, Liofilizada, or any white granulated sugar.
ingredients.substitution: Sugar is functionally essential to foam stability. Do not substitute in core.
ingredients.ratioAdjustment: If reducing, expect less stable foam and paler crust.
ingredients.expectedEffect: Stable ribbon-stage foam; deep golden-amber crust matching target.
ingredients.newRisk: Excess sugar -> collapse; deficit -> pale, dense crumb.
ingredients.omissionResult: Foam will not stabilize; product fails.

ingredients.name: Whole eggs (room temp)
ingredients.function: Primary structure + leavening (foam) + moisture + color (yolk fat & lecithin).
ingredients.evidence: Canonical bizcochuelo; family statement "todo a base de huevos frescos"; foam-only published recipes.
ingredients.supermarketOption: Any supermarket brand (e.g. San Fernando, Pehuen). Medium-large (~60 g shell-on).
ingredients.substitution: None in core. Separated-egg method is a diagnostic variant, not a substitution.

ingredients.name: Applewood / algarrobo wood smoke (surface exposure)
ingredients.function: Smoke aroma on crust from algarrobo lambayecano wood combustion.
ingredients.evidence: CONFIRMED: Multiple independent sources state "La leña que se usa es algarrobo lambayecano, que le da un aromo y sabor peculiar." Food science (PMC, MDPI) confirms wood-smoke phenols adsorb to baked goods. Upgraded from speculative to diagnostic — the wood IS used, but perceptibility in the finished clamshell-packaged product still needs a triangle test.
ingredients.supermarketOption: Smoking chips (applewood imported; algarrobo wood regional).
ingredients.expectedEffect: Faint smoke note on crust from algarrobo phenols.
ingredients.newRisk: Overpowering smoke; food-safety concerns if uncontrolled.

ingredients.name: Baking powder (low dose)
ingredients.evidence: None direct for Valera. Tested only if foam-only control fails to reach target rise.
ingredients.ratioAdjustment: Start at 1-1.5% baker%; increase only if justified.
ingredients.expectedEffect: Extra oven spring; risk of coarser crumb and chemical taste.

ingredients.name: Neutral oil (trace)
ingredients.evidence: None direct for Valera. Chiffon-style addition; tested only if crumb is too dry on day two.
ingredients.substitution: Melted butter adds flavor but changes texture.
ingredients.ratioAdjustment: Reduce sugar slightly if adding fat.
ingredients.expectedEffect: Moister crumb; slightly less foam volume.

ingredients.name: Vanilla extract
ingredients.evidence: Common in modern recipes; NOT advertised on label; not in family statements.
ingredients.substitution: Citrus zest (lime or orange) — regional alternative.

ingredients.name: 10 g baking powder (as in previous report)
ingredients.function: Rejected: dose was unjustified and likely excessive.
ingredients.evidence: Previous report. No foam-only control was tested. 4.2% baker% is high and risks chemical taste.
ingredients.substitution: Use foam-only or low-dose diagnostic instead.

ingredients.name: Algarrobina (carob syrup)
ingredients.evidence: Regional northern-Peru ingredient. The deep color COULD be algarrobina OR pure Maillard. No producer confirmation.
ingredients.newRisk: Off-flavor if overdosed; contradicts "pure egg" claim.
ingredients.omissionResult: Color from Maillard alone (the core target).

ingredients.name: Cake flour / lower-protein flour
ingredients.evidence: Food science: lower protein = less gluten = more tender.
ingredients.supermarketOption: Harina para pastelería (look for "harina 0000" or low-protein brands in Wong/Tottus).
ingredients.newRisk: May be weaker structurally; fold gently.

ingredients.name: Potato starch (chuño / fécula de papa)
ingredients.function: Tenderizes crumb by diluting gluten; absorbs water; delays staling.
ingredients.evidence: Traditional Andean ingredient; modern Peruvian recipes use ~10% of flour weight.
ingredients.supermarketOption: Fécula de papa (look in market aisles or buy chuño and grind/sift finely).
ingredients.substitution: Cornstarch (maicena) is a partial substitute but gelatinizes at a lower temperature and gives a slightly different mouthfeel.
ingredients.ratioAdjustment: Replace up to 10% of flour weight 1:1.
ingredients.expectedEffect: Softer, finer crumb; longer shelf life.

techniques.name: Weigh eggs (shelled) rather than count
techniques.function: Eliminates egg-size variation, the largest source of ratio drift.
techniques.targetEvidence: Eggs vary 50-70 g; 8 eggs can shift the formula by ±20%.
techniques.simplerAlternative: Counting eggs is simpler but imprecise.
techniques.failureMode: Counting leads to dense or collapsed bakes.

techniques.name: Whip whole eggs + sugar to ribbon stage ("punto cinta")
techniques.function: Primary leavening; traps air; stabilizes foam.
techniques.targetEvidence: Canonical bizcochuelo technique; visible fine-even crumb in target.
techniques.simplerAlternative: None — this IS the simplest leavening method for a fat-free sponge.
techniques.failureMode: Underwhipping -> dense; overwhipping -> coarse, fragile foam.
techniques.measurement: Ribbon trail holds 3-second figure-8; volume tripled; pale ivory.

techniques.name: Sift dry ingredients once
techniques.simplerAlternative: Whisking in a bowl is equivalent for dispersion.
techniques.failureMode: Multiple sifts add steps without measurable benefit.

techniques.name: Fold dry into foam in 3 additions
techniques.measurement: No dry streaks; batter still voluminous.

techniques.name: Grease + parchment-line mold bottom only; sides ungreased
techniques.function: Allows batter to grip sides and climb (oven spring); parchment ensures clean release.
techniques.targetEvidence: Standard sponge practice; matches the straight-sided target.
techniques.simplerAlternative: Greasing sides — simpler but reduces rise.

techniques.name: Bake at 180°C, ~22-26 min for individual molds
techniques.function: Sets foam before it collapses; develops Maillard crust.
techniques.targetEvidence: Published foam-only recipes; target color indicates moderate-high heat.
techniques.failureMode: Too hot -> dark crust before crumb sets; too cool -> collapse.

techniques.name: Cool 5 min in mold, then invert/unmold onto rack
techniques.function: Prevents steam-softening the crust; sets structure.
techniques.failureMode: Unmolding too hot -> tearing; leaving in mold too long -> gummy base.

techniques.name: Warm whole eggs to ~38-40°C before whipping
techniques.function: Lowers surface tension, accelerates foam formation, increases final volume.
techniques.targetEvidence: Standard genoise practice; foam reaches ribbon stage faster.
techniques.simplerAlternative: Room-temp eggs (already specified) whip adequately with 1-2 extra minutes.

techniques.name: Tap mold once on counter
techniques.function: Releases large trapped air pockets that would form tunnels.

techniques.name: Optional: baking stone / deck-heat simulation
techniques.function: Mimics the strong bottom heat of a wood-fired clay deck.
techniques.targetEvidence: Wood oven has high thermal-mass floor.
techniques.simplerAlternative: A preheated heavy sheet pan on the lower rack.

techniques.name: Three-time sifting of flour
techniques.function: Rejected: no measurable improvement over one thorough sift.
techniques.failureMode: Adds time during which foam waits and deflates.

techniques.name: Combining whole-egg AND separated-egg methods in one recipe
techniques.function: Rejected: confounds the variable; adds steps and collapse risk.
techniques.targetEvidence: Previous report presented both as a single hybrid.
techniques.failureMode: Hybrid collapses more easily than either pure method.

techniques.name: Adding baking powder "for reliability"
techniques.function: Rejected: no foam-only control was tested first.

techniques.name: Smoke exposure before unsmoked control
techniques.function: Rejected sequence: must establish unsmoked baseline first.

techniques.name: Treat algarrobina as equivalent to algarrobo wood smoke
techniques.function: Rejected: syrup flavor ≠ combustion smoke aroma.

techniques.name: Rest batter before baking
techniques.function: Rejected: deflates foam with no benefit.

substitutions.propertyLost: Algarrobina has a distinct carob flavor; chancaca is more caramel
substitutions.techniqueAdjustment: Dissolve into egg foam at ribbon stage
Fold even more gently; do not overmix.

substitutions.propertyLost: Some gluten strength; chuño has a slightly earthy note

substitutions.substitute: Preheated heavy sheet pan on lower rack
substitutions.propertyLost: Less thermal mass than a stone
Chuño gelatinizes at higher temp; cornstarch gives a slightly softer, shorter crumb
substitutions.techniqueAdjustment: None, but expect marginally different mouthfeel

substitutions.propertyLost: Sweet vanillin note; zest adds oil-soluble terpenes
substitutions.techniqueAdjustment: Rub into sugar before whipping to release oils

substitutions.propertyLost: Simplicity; one extra bowl; higher collapse risk
substitutions.techniqueAdjustment: Beat yolks + sugar to ribbon; whip whites to soft peaks; fold whites in 3 additions

substitutions.substitute: Conventional home oven + stone + optional smoke treatment
substitutions.techniqueAdjustment: Use stone; test smoke as a separate variant only after unsmoked control

recipes.name: Core Best-Evidence Recipe (Foam-Only Control)
recipes.summary: The minimal egg–sugar–flour–salt sponge. No chemical leavener, no starch, no fat, no flavoring. The baseline against which every other variant is compared.
recipes.question: What is the smallest formula that plausibly reproduces the target?
recipes.expectedEffect: Fine, even, golden-amber crumb with a tender crust and clean egg aroma; individual round domed cakes.
recipes.successCriterion: Visible fine crumb; dome intact; deep golden-amber top; clean egg aroma; no chemical taste; no collapse; day-two texture still acceptable.
recipes.abandonmentCriterion: Collapse, dense lower layer, gummy center, or pale color after two controlled attempts.

recipes.yieldNote: 6 individual round domed cakes (~6.5 cm dia × ~3.5 cm tall), ~75 g each. Scale up linearly for 16-piece packs.
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C (convection) or 190°C (static). Place a heavy baking sheet or stone on the lower rack to preheat.
Grease 6 individual round molds (~7 cm dia, ~4 cm tall) and line bottoms with parchment. Do NOT grease the sides — the batter must grip to climb.
In a heatproof bowl, combine whole eggs + sugar. Warm gently over a water bath to ~38°C, stirring, then remove from heat.
Whip on high speed until pale, thick, tripled in volume, and a ribbon trail holds a 3-second figure-8 (~6-8 min).
Sift flour + salt once directly over the foam.
Fold in 3 additions using a wide spatula: cut down the middle, scrape along the bottom, lift up and over. Stop the instant no dry streaks remain.
Divide batter into molds (~75 g each). Tap each mold once on the counter to release large bubbles.
Bake on the middle rack 22-26 min. Do NOT open the door before 20 min.
Done when: top is deep golden-amber, a toothpick comes out clean, internal temp ~95°C, and the surface springs back.
Cool 5 min in the mold, then run a thin blade around (sides only) and invert onto a rack. Cool fully before packaging.

recipes.name: Diagnostic A — Chuño vs Cornstarch
recipes.summary: Controlled single-variable test: replace cornstarch with an equal weight of potato starch (chuño).
recipes.question: Does chuño produce a measurably different crumb than cornstarch?
recipes.mainVariable: Starch type (chuño vs cornstarch) at 10% of flour weight.
recipes.expectedEffect: Chuño: slightly higher gelatinization temp, marginally firmer bite, faintly earthier note.
recipes.successCriterion: Blind triangle test: can a taster distinguish chuño from cornstarch above chance?
recipes.abandonmentCriterion: No perceptible difference -> keep the more available starch (cornstarch).
recipes.yieldNote: 6 cakes — bake control and diagnostic side by side.
steps: Identical to Lima substitution variant.

recipes.name: Diagnostic B — Whole-Egg vs Separated-Egg Foam
recipes.summary: Controlled test: separated-egg method (yolks+ sugar ribbon, whites whipped separately, folded).
recipes.question: Does separated-egg method yield higher volume or finer crumb than whole-egg whipping?
recipes.expectedEffect: Greater volume; potentially coarser cells; one extra bowl and step.
recipes.successCriterion: Measurably higher dome AND equal-or-better crumb fineness.
recipes.abandonmentCriterion: Higher dome but coarser crumb -> reject; keep whole-egg core.

research.findings: Chuño (freeze-dried potato starch) tenderizes crumb by diluting gluten; modern Peruvian home recipes use ~10% of flour weight. Cornstarch is a partial substitute but gelatinizes differently. Vanilla is common in modern recipes but absent from the label and not advertised. Whole-egg whipping to "punto cinta" (ribbon stage) is the canonical technique. Warming whole eggs to ~40°C accelerates foam but is optional. Separated-egg method gives more volume but adds steps.

research.findings: Traditional Peruvian bizcochuelo recipes (Todos Santos, Yanuq) commonly use cornstarch (maicena) at 10-50% of flour weight. The Yanuq recipe (6 eggs separated, ½ cup flour, ½ cup chuño, 1 tsp baking powder) is the canonical modern hybrid — confirms our rejection of hybrid + leavener in the core.
